title: Control Plane Kickstart: Lab Report & Commissioning Playbook
content:
Purpose and scope
This is a lab-first commissioning report and short runbook for initial control-plane (CP) setup in customer VPCs and air-gapped on-prem environments. Focus: fast, repeatable kickstart, safe scale/rotation patterns, and Terraform module gotchas observed in the lab. Not the canonical operator guide — this is a practical field report with commands, example TF snippets, and decision checkpoints.

Executive summary (quick)
- Successfully bootstrapped a minimal CP with HA control-plane services + etcd raft in a 3-node on-prem LAB.
- Discovered two TF module friction points (networking variables and dynamic node labels) and one upgrade ordering hazard (etcd snapshot timing).
- Proposed safe upgrade waves: control-plane services -> connectors -> worker nodes, with KV cache warm restart and KMS key rotation window.

Prereqs (lab and customer)
- Admin access to target VPC / on-prem staging VLANs, jumpbox SSH, and KMS access.
- Terraform v1.5.9, terragrunt used in some customers (note differences below).
- kubectl (1.26 compatible), ssh keypair, and a bench node for load tests.

Quick kickoff checklist (1h):
- Validate network CIDRs and reserve /30 for heartbeat between CP nodes.
- Confirm NAT routes for outbound artifact fetch (or prepare airgap bundles).
- Provision KMS key ARN and test encrypt/decrypt using customer KMS shim.
- Apply minimal TF to create controlplane primaries (see tf-snippet).

Terraform module notes (observed)
- Module: redwood/private-controlplane (v0.9.x in lab)
  - var.network_whitelist expects comma-separated string, but example used list -> caused plan diffs. Wrap with join(",", var.networks) or update callers.
  - node_labels variable is map(string) but we often want dynamic kubelet labels per instance group. We added optional var.extra_node_labels_json to pass through JSON string for edge cases.
  - etcd_snapshot_schedule: module creates a cron on the primary node. During upgrade we observed snapshot race if snapshot executed while etcd peers were restarting. Add a pre-upgrade hook to pause snapshots for 5m.

TF example (lab snippet)
- note: environment-specific values removed
resource "module" "cp_core" {
  source = "../../modules/private-controlplane"
  cluster_name = var.cluster_name
  network_whitelist = join(",", var.allowed_networks)
  node_count = 3
  etcd_snapshot_schedule = "0 */6 * * *"
  extra_node_labels_json = jsonencode({ role = "controlplane" })
}

Bootstrap commands (sequence)
1) terraform init
2) terraform apply -target=module.cp_core.bootstrap -var 'cluster_name=lab-01'
3) ssh to primary and verify etcd members: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl member list --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 
4) ensure API server health: kubectl --kubeconfig=/etc/redwood/kubeconfig get componentstatus

Scaling playbook (adding worker pools)
- Scale step: add worker instance group with distinct labels and instance types (ex: gpus vs cpu). Apply TF with -target=module.worker_pools["gpu"].
- Validate autoscaler metrics; run a synthetic workload to warm KV cache and model caches (rerun typical request patterns).
- Autoscaler quirks: small bursty requests may cause overprovision if metrics window too small. We set scale_down_unneeded_time to 15m in lab.

Upgrade plan (safe waves)
- Wave 0: Preflight checks (versions, snapshots, slack notif)
- Wave 1 (Canary CP): Upgrade 1 controlplane node -> run health probes 10m -> promote if healthy
- Wave 2 (Remaining CP): Rolling restarts of remaining CP nodes with etcd snapshot pause and kv-cache flush after last node returns
- Wave 3 (Infrastructure): Upgrade ingress / load-balancer, storage drivers
- Wave 4 (Workers): Rolling upgrade of worker pools by instance-group; maintain >=1 worker on previous version during canary tests
- Wave 5 (Post): KMS key rotation (see KMS rotation window) and cleanup.

Commands and safety knobs for upgrade
- Pause etcd snapshots: touch /var/run/etcd.pause && systemctl restart etcd-snapshot-cron || set cron-disabled flag
- To upgrade single CP node: drain local workloads, apply TF changes scoped to that node, wait for node to rejoin etcd and verify member list
- Member verification: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl endpoint status --write-out=table --endpoints=$(cat /etc/redwood/etcd_endpoints)

KMS rotation window (recommended)
- Rotate keys only after all components can read both old and new envelope keys. Two-step approach:
  1) Add new key as secondary (roll to accept new key).
  2) After 24h of dual-read validation, promote new key and deprecate old.
- Fail-safe: keep last-good backup of cluster secrets (encrypted) outside CP for 30 days.

KV cache / prefix cache considerations
- Don't purge KV cache immediately after upgrade; allow warm retries for 30 mins. If inconsistent results are detected (model version mismatch), run staged cache invalidation per model-route.

Rollback heuristics (fast)
- If control-plane API error rates > 5% sustained for 10m AND latency > 2x baseline: trigger rollback to previous terraform state for modules.cp_core (use terraform state pull to get previous artifact).
- For etcd quorum loss: follow recovery doc (confluence link above) to restore from snapshot and re-add members.

Lab failure notes (lessons)
- Observed flaky API early: caused by mismatch in envoy config generation due to node-label schema change. Fix: add backward-compatible label translation in configgen.
- Terraform drift: dynamic hostnames created outside TF produced repeated apply diffs. Always wrap provider-created resources in TF or mark as external resources with lifecycle.ignore_changes.

Open questions / followups
- Should we standardize on json-encoded node labels in the module interface to avoid downstream ambiguity? (Samir to propose RFC)
- Add pre-upgrade synthetic smoke tests into the console pipeline? (PR referenced)
- Need clearer guidance when customers use Terragrunt layering — some refactors in modules required.

Attachments and artifacts
- Lab logs: s3://redwood-lab-logs/cp-kickstart-2025-01-12/ (internal)
- Test PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4891
- Jira ticket capturing followups: INF-1423

Quick appendix: useful commands
- terraform plan -var-file=env.staging.tfvars -out=plan.out
- terraform apply plan.out
- etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap.db --endpoints=$(cat /etc/redwood/etcd_endpoints)
- kubectl get pods -A --kubeconfig=/etc/redwood/kubeconfig | grep -E "controlplane|etcd|api-server"

Author notes (free-form)
- This doc is intentionally workshop/lab flavored — aim to convert the stable patterns here into a condensed operator-runbook (single-page) and a terraform-module RFC.
- Tagging for next sprint: module API cleanup, snapshot pause helper script, and terragrunt compatibility test matrix.

End of document
